subject: SummitWare renewal - proposed rate rebalance & uplift pathway
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Jacob Liao <jacob.liao@summitware.com>
Cc: Ellen Park <ellen.park@summitware.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SummitWare renewal - proposed rate rebalance & uplift pathway

Hi Jacob / Ellen,

Thanks again for the time earlier this week. Per our conversation I’m sharing a concise renewal proposal that aims to: preserve unit economics for SummitWare as usage grows, provide a short-term price hold to avoid churn, and create a clear uplift path if you commit to the higher-tier capacity over the next 12 months.

Key points in the attached summary: the base per-token rate would adjust to reflect the new reserved commit mix (monthly committed tokens + burst pool). We can offer a 6-month price hold on the base rate if SummitWare signs a 12-month renewal and commits to a 20% uplift in committed monthly tokens by month 3.

Concessions we can provide now:
- $120k one-time credit applied across months 1-3 after renewal (to smooth migration costs).
- A capped per-month burst allowance (100M tokens/mo) at the lower committed rate for the first 90 days post-signature.
- Priority routing and two emergency capacity bursts per year at no additional charge (subject to notice).

Open items for your team:
1) Confirm whether the 20% uplift commitment is acceptable as a condition for the 6-month price hold.
2) If procurement requires, we can convert the one-time credit into a multi-month monthly credit schedule.
3) Any SOC2 / audit evidence required to include with procurement.

I’ve attached the renewal_summary.pdf and a pricing_model_breakdown.xlsx for your procurement team. If this looks reasonable, I’ll loop in Neha to finalize the contract language and get a DocuSign ready.

Thanks,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0139

Attachment: 2027-04-07_summitware_renewal_summary.pdf (pdf)
Attachment: 2027-04-07_pricing_model_breakdown.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Jacob Liao <jacob.liao@summitware.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Ellen Park <ellen.park@summitware.com>, finance@summitware.com
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SummitWare renewal - proposed rate rebalance & uplift pathway

Vivek —

Appreciate the clear summary. A few high-level items from our side after a quick review with finance and product: we like the concept of a price hold but can’t commit to a 20% uplift by month 3 — that timeline is aggressive given our product roadmap and Q3 launches. We could consider a stepped uplift (10% by month 3, 25% by month 6) tied to specific adoption milestones.

On credits: converting the $120k into a 6-month amortized credit would help our monthly budgeting. Also requesting a 9-month price hold rather than 6 months if we agree to the stepped uplift schedule.

Procurement has two asks:
- A clause allowing a one-time true-up after month 6 if actual committed usage diverges >20% from the forecast.
- Evidence of log retention and access to token-level cost reporting for our finance audit.

Can you confirm whether the stepped uplift + 9-month hold + amortized credits are feasible? If so we’ll circulate internally and aim to return a clean PO within 10 business days.

Thanks,
Jacob
Jacob Liao
VP of Platform, SummitWare
jacob.liao@summitware.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: SummitWare renewal - pricing asks (need guidance)

Team —

Looping you in. SummitWare is pushing for a less aggressive uplift timeline and wants a 9-month price hold if we accept a stepped uplift (10% by M3, 25% by M6). They also want the $120k credit amortized over 6 months and a contractual true-up clause after month 6. Procurement also wants token-level reporting access.

Questions:
- Margin impact: is the stepped uplift + 9-month hold materially worse than our original ask? I ran a sensitivity but want your view before we finalize concessions.
- Is converting the $120k credit into 6 monthly credits acceptable from finance?
- Can we add a contractual true-up that is revenue-neutral if they miss the uplift target (e.g., pro-rated credits reversed)?

I attached the pricing_model_breakdown.xlsx. Please reply with a recommended concession list and any required legal language. Hope to respond to SummitWare by Friday EOD.

Thanks,
Vivek

Attachment: 2027-04-07_pricing_model_breakdown.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 16:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SummitWare renewal - pricing asks (need guidance)

Vivek —

Reviewed with finance and legal. Recommendation below so we can close quickly: 

1) Accept the stepped uplift cadence: 10% committed uplift by month 3, 25% by month 6. Tie each step to a measurable adoption milestone (new feature X usage >= 5% of total requests; or monthly active product seats >= N).
2) Offer a 9-month price hold on the base rate, but only if the signed SOW includes the stepped uplift and an annual minimum commitment recalculated accordingly. If they fail to hit the milestones, the price hold reverts and a pro-rated credit reversal applies (contract language provided by legal).
3) Convert the $120k into a 6-month amortized credit (credits applied month 1-6). Finance agrees this smooths their cash flow and keeps our cash recognition predictable.
4) Add the true-up clause after month 6: a one-time reconciliation where we compare forecast vs actual and apply an agreed pro-rate formula. If SummitWare is below forecast by >20%, they owe the pro-rated difference or forfeit remaining credits; if they're above, we credit them retroactively.
5) Token-level reporting: product can expose read-only cost and token logs via a secure link; legal to include a limited-access clause to satisfy their audit.

If you want, I’ll draft the contract bullets and loop legal (Aditya, please advise on the reversal wording and any redlines). From a margin standpoint the stepped uplift + 9-month hold is acceptable given the amortized credit and the reconciliation clause — we preserve upside if they grow.

Neha
Neha Kapoor
VP, Commercial Finance, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
